say: This BMW is one metre off Gary's bumper. At *seventy.* And it's about to get worse.
Dual carriageway. Seventy limit. Gary's in the right lane, overtaking a line of *lorries.* Doing exactly seventy.
Then, Brandon. Black BMW. He comes up fast, and sits right on Gary's *bumper.*
One metre. At seventy miles an hour. If Gary brakes, there's *no* time to stop.
Then the full beams. Flash. Flash. Flash. *Move* *over!*
But Gary *can't* move over. The lorries are still on his left.
So Gary does what a lot of us *want* to do. He taps the brakes. *Hard.*
Brandon locks up, and *swerves.* Inches from a crash.
And three cars back, a *police* car saw the lot. It pulls them *both* over.
Rule one two six. Leave at least a *two* *second* gap. Tailgating can be careless driving. A hundred pound fine and three points.
And rule one one zero. Only flash your headlights to let others know you're there. *Never* to intimidate.
But braking hard to teach him a *lesson?* That can cause the very crash Gary was worried about. It can count as careless driving *too.*
The right move? Ease off *gently,* finish the overtake, then move left, and let him go.
Brandon, *guilty.* Gary, *half* *right.* Would you have tapped the brakes? Follow for case seven.
